title: Dementia Clinical Evidence Blueprint v1
description: Extension-only manifest. Does NOT create a new disease, new FAST stages, or new PPS/KPS definitions -- 'Dementia Due To Alzheimer's Disease' under the Neurologic System / Degenerative Brain Disorders family already exists (PR #44, merged) with its own self-contained FAST Stage 7 variant and KPS/PPS/ADL HOSPICE_ELIGIBILITY_SUPPORT concepts, plus every one of the major complications the source guidance identifies (Aspiration Pneumonia, Pyelonephritis, Septicemia [clinically equivalent to Sepsis], Stage 3-4 Pressure Ulcers, Recurrent Fever After Antibiotics, Ten Percent Weight Loss In Six Months [clinically equivalent to >10% weight loss], Serum Albumin Less Than 2.5 g/dL). This manifest adds only what PR #44 does not already contain: (1) 7 missing atomic dementia concepts (Six Or Fewer Intelligible Words, Progressive Ambulation Loss, Progressive Transfer Dependence, Progressive Feeding Dependence, Progressive Weight Loss, Nonspecific Nutritional Decline, Recurrent Aspiration Events) with provenance metadata; (2) three cross-disease OntologyRelationship edges linking Dementia's existing FAST Stage 7 / PPS Less Than 70 Percent / KPS Less Than 70 Percent concepts to the corresponding Functional Assessment Framework v1 (PR #49, merged) scale-definition concepts, so a nurse viewing Dementia evidence can navigate to the full scale interpretation without any assessment definition ever being duplicated; (3) a recertification evidence trend model (10 PROGNOSTIC_INDICATOR concepts covering FAST/PPS/KPS/Speech/Ambulation/Transfer/Weight/Nutrition/Complication History/Narrative trend) for Dementia; (4) a documentation-only AI capability boundary (ai_may / ai_may_not), mirroring the pattern already established in the Functional Assessment Framework v1 and CHF Clinical Evidence Blueprint v1 manifests. No schema, migration, or API changes. No existing PR #44 or PR #49 row is ever modified, renamed, or duplicated.

already_present_verified.note: Every major complication requested for this PR was verified already present in PR #44 under a clinically-equivalent name. No duplicate concept was created for any of these.

mapping.existing_concept: Stage 3 Pressure Ulcer / Stage 4 Pressure Ulcer
Ten Percent Weight Loss In Six Months

new_concepts.name: Six Or Fewer Intelligible Words
new_concepts.description: A more specific, granular verbal-communication criterion than the existing 'No Consistently Meaningful Verbal Communication' finding: the patient's vocabulary has declined to six or fewer intelligible, distinguishable words over the course of an average day.

new_concepts.name: Progressive Ambulation Loss
new_concepts.description: A progression-over-time pattern of declining ambulatory ability (rather than the existing point-in-time 'Unable To Ambulate Without Assistance' finding), supporting functional-decline documentation across serial assessments.

new_concepts.name: Progressive Transfer Dependence
new_concepts.description: A progression-over-time pattern of increasing dependence on others for transfers (bed-to-chair, sit-to-stand), not previously modeled in the existing Dementia concept set.

new_concepts.name: Progressive Feeding Dependence
new_concepts.description: A progression-over-time pattern of increasing dependence on others for feeding, not previously modeled in the existing Dementia concept set.

new_concepts.name: Progressive Weight Loss
new_concepts.description: An ongoing, progression-over-time pattern of weight loss (distinct from the existing point-in-time 'Ten Percent Weight Loss In Six Months' threshold finding), supporting trend documentation across serial assessments.

new_concepts.name: Nonspecific Nutritional Decline
new_concepts.description: General, non-threshold-based nutritional decline (reduced intake, declining oral acceptance) that may precede or accompany measurable weight loss, relevant to the complete clinical picture even before a specific percentage or lab threshold is met.

new_concepts.name: Recurrent Aspiration Events
new_concepts.description: Repeated episodes of aspiration (coughing/choking with oral intake or witnessed aspiration) that may or may not progress to aspiration pneumonia, distinct from the existing 'Aspiration Pneumonia' complication concept.

functional_assessment_linkage.description: Links Dementia's existing FAST Stage 7 finding to the Functional Assessment Framework's FAST scale definition for full nurse-facing score interpretation, without duplicating the scale's level content.

Links Dementia's existing PPS Less Than 70 Percent hospice-eligibility-support concept to the Functional Assessment Framework's PPS scale definition for full nurse-facing score interpretation, without duplicating the scale's level content.

Links Dementia's existing KPS Less Than 70 Percent hospice-eligibility-support concept to the Functional Assessment Framework's KPS scale definition for full nurse-facing score interpretation, without duplicating the scale's level content.

trend_indicators.name: FAST Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous FAST stage to the current FAST stage at recertification; a worsening (higher) stage supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: PPS Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous PPS score to the current PPS score at recertification; a decreasing score supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: KPS Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's previous KPS score to the current KPS score at recertification; a decreasing score supports continued functional-decline documentation.

trend_indicators.name: Speech Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's verbal communication ability between the previous and current certification periods, documenting progressive loss of meaningful speech.

trend_indicators.name: Ambulation Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's ambulatory ability between the previous and current certification periods, documenting progressive ambulation loss.

trend_indicators.name: Transfer Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's transfer ability between the previous and current certification periods, documenting progressive transfer dependence.

trend_indicators.name: Weight Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's weight between the previous and current certification periods, documenting unintentional weight loss.

trend_indicators.name: Nutrition Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the patient's oral intake and nutritional status between the previous and current certification periods.

trend_indicators.name: Complication History Trend
trend_indicators.description: Comparison of the frequency and severity of complications (aspiration events, infections, pressure ulcers) between the previous and current certification periods.

trend_indicators.name: Narrative Trend
trend_indicators.description: A structured narrative summary comparing the patient's overall clinical course between the previous and current certification periods, supporting the physician's recertification determination.

differentiation_guards: This manifest never creates a new OntologyDisease, OntologyDiseaseFamily, or OntologyBodySystem row -- it resolves the existing Dementia Due To Alzheimer's Disease disease and the existing Functional Assessment Framework disease by exact name and aborts if either is missing.
This manifest never creates a new OntologyDiseaseVariant row (no new FAST stages).
This manifest never creates a duplicate FAST/PPS/KPS definition -- it links to PR #44's and PR #49's existing rows via OntologyRelationship only.
This manifest never duplicates a major complication already present in PR #44 -- see already_present_verified.mapping for the exact clinically-equivalent existing concept each requested item maps to.

Dementia clinical evidence and functional assessments support functional status documentation, clinical decline documentation, recertification review, and clinical picture development; they do not independently establish diagnosis, prognosis, hospice eligibility, or terminal status.
